context: This IEEE 754 single-precision number occupies 4 bytes. The 32 cells in the diagram run from bit 31 on the left to bit 0 on the right. Braces mark the sign S in orange, the exponent E in blue, and the fraction N in green.
description: The table first lists the fields and their stored values. Bit positions are numbered from 0 at the right. The labels b31, b30, b23, b22, and b0 mark the corresponding field boundaries.

frames.explanation: E is between 1 and 254, so use the formula for a normal number. The sign factor is +1. The actual exponent is 124 − 127 = −3, so the scale factor is 2 to the power of −3, or 0.125. In the fraction field, only the second and third bits after the binary point are 1. Thus N = 2 to the power of −2 plus 2 to the power of −3, or 0.375. Adding the implicit leading 1 gives 1.375. Multiplying the three factors gives 1 × 0.125 × 1.375 = 0.171875, matching the result at the lower right of the figure.
frames.title: Bit fields of a single-precision floating-point number

result: The formula for a normal number is (−1)^S × 2^(E−127) × (1+N). Values with E equal to 0 or 255 follow special rules for zero, subnormal numbers, infinity, and NaN, so this formula does not apply directly. The exponent increases range without increasing precision. A normal number has 23 fraction bits plus the implicit 1, for 24 bits of binary precision. As the absolute value increases, the spacing between adjacent representable numbers generally grows.
summary: Split the 32-bit encoding into sign, exponent, and fraction, then calculate its value.
